subject: maths
question: I bought two bicycles for ₹1,200. I sold the first one at a loss of 9% and the second at a gain of 27%. If, on the whole I made neither a loss nor a gain, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first bicycle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By Alligation, compare individual profit/loss percentages with the net overall percentage.

Loss on 1st = −9%, Gain on 2nd = +27%, Net = 0%.

Ratio of Cost Prices = (27 − 0) : (0 − (−9)) = 27 : 9 = 3 : 1.

Total CP parts = 3 + 1 = 4 parts → ₹1200.

CP of the 1st bicycle = (3 ÷ 4) × 1200 = ₹900.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Cost Price of two bicycles = ₹1200

Loss on 1st bicycle = 9%

Gain on 2nd bicycle = 27%

Overall net profit or loss = 0%

 0 − (−9) = 9
 Ratio = 27 : 9 = 3 : 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let CP of 1st bicycle = x and CP of 2nd bicycle = y

⇒ Since net profit/loss is 0, Loss amount on 1st = Profit amount on 2nd

⇒ 9% of x = 27% of y

⇒ 0.09 × x = 0.27 × y

⇒ x ÷ y = 27 ÷ 9 = 3 ÷ 1

⇒ Ratio of CP (x : y) = 3 : 1

⇒ Total parts = 3 + 1 = 4 parts

⇒ 4 parts = ₹1200

⇒ 1 part = 1200 ÷ 4 = ₹300

⇒ CP of 1st bicycle (x) = 3 × 300 = ₹900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Overall No Profit No Loss

When a transaction results in neither a profit nor a loss, the absolute profit earned on one item is exactly equal to the absolute loss incurred on the other: Profit % × CP₁ = Loss % × CP₂.

Alligation in Profit & Loss

Alligation gives the direct ratio of Cost Prices when the profit/loss percentages of individual parts and the overall profit/loss percentage are combined.
